title: Reverse String
description: Reverse a string in-place using two pointers. Compare built-in reverse with manual pointer swap and recursive reversal.

data.text: Write a function that reverses a string. The input string is given as an array of characters `s`. You must do this by modifying the input array in-place with O(1) extra memory.
The simplest solution uses the built-in `Array.Reverse`. This is the most readable but least educational approach.

data.title: Note
data.text: `Array.Reverse` is in-place and O(n) time, O(1) space. In production code, prefer this unless you need a custom algorithm.
Use two pointers starting at both ends of the array and swap elements while moving inward. This is the canonical interview answer.

data.title: Two-Pointer O(n) — Interview Optimal
What improved here?
data.text: **Readability:** Tuple swap `(a, b) = (b, a)` replaces the traditional temp variable pattern, reducing lines and eliminating a local variable. **Performance:** Same O(n) time, O(1) space as built-in. This approach demonstrates the two-pointer pattern clearly for interviewers.
Recursion can solve this but requires O(n) call stack space, violating the O(1) space constraint. Still useful for understanding recursion patterns.

data.title: Recursive O(n) time, O(n) space
When not to use
data.text: Recursion adds stack overhead. For very large strings (e.g., 10^4 chars), you risk a stack overflow. The iterative two-pointer approach is safer.
